description: Does conjugation parity constrain the A=3 (Borromean) magnitude gap (c₃=0.63×μ₃, ~1.6× near-miss)? NO. The n=9 structure is 30 partitions = 14 conjugate pairs + 2 self-conjugate {(5,1,1,1,1),(3,3,3)}, sgn=+1 (opposite of the deuteron; self-conjugate feeds bar-even, symmetric Δ_λ NOT excluded). Two reasons parity cannot touch the magnitude: (R1) parity is a RELABELING not a rescaling — it sorts terms into channels but each contributes its full derived amount, so it supplies no coefficient; (R2) the gap lives at the BARE single-trace level (1−τ_Borr=h⁴(3+h²)/(h²+4), proved) not the Δ_λ-dressing level where parity acts. VERDICT (scope-a negative): conjugation parity is orthogonal to the A=3 magnitude — it narrows the weight class (GAP-1) but cannot supply the ~1.6×; the magnitude stays the Track-A gate. Closes the route. scope-(a), audit-only, nothing wired; no fit.
tier: scope-(a) honest negative (exact n=9 structure + two orthogonality arguments); no fit

n9_conjugation_structure.meaning: n=9 ⇒ sgn=+1 (opposite of deuteron n=6): self-conjugate feeds bar-EVEN, and a conjugation-symmetric Δ_λ is NOT excluded (GAP-1 gives no exclusion at A=3).

R1_parity_is_relabeling_not_rescaling.statement: the signed parity map sorts terms into channels; each partition contributes its full derived amount. Parity fixes the channel, never the magnitude ⇒ no coefficient, so the ~1.6× cannot come from parity.

R2_gap_is_bare_trace_level.statement: the A=3 gap (c₃=0.63×μ₃, μ₃=+0.4708) is a property of the BARE single Markov trace; the Δ_λ per-partition dressing (where conjugation parity acts) is a different downstream object the gap does not enter.

verdict.classification: scope-(a) honest negative: conjugation parity is ORTHOGONAL to the A=3 magnitude — it narrows the weight class (GAP-1) but supplies no coefficient. The ~1.6× remains the standing Track-A magnitude gate.
verdict.closes_route: using parity to constrain the A=3 magnitude — do not re-try.
